title: Trace retention-hint router for Tempo tiering and on-call escalation
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Background: Some tenants ingest high-cardinality traces that should be retained longer for debugging, while others prefer low-cost short retention. Tempo currently accepts OTLP spans but lacks a first-class, tenant-driven retention hint mapping. Problem: without a retention hint router, we need heavyweight workarounds (per-tenant Tempo instances or manual archive jobs) that increase cost and operational burden. Goal: implement a routing component that reads a tenant/trace-level retention_hint (OTLP resource/span attribute and optional HTTP header), maps it to Tempo storage tiers (hot/warm/archival), annotates spans with the target retention tier, and emits control events for on-call escalation when unusually long retention requests appear. This component must be backward-compatible (default to normal retention) and operate with minimal added latency on the OTLP ingestion path.
acceptance_criteria: Router reads retention_hint from OTLP resource.attributes 'redwood.retain_for' and from X-Redwood-Retention HTTP header, with header taking precedence when present.
Retention hints are mapped to Tempo internal tier tags (hot, 30d, 90d, archive) and added as span/envelope attributes before Tempo ingestion.
If a tenant requests retention beyond their quota, router emits an alert event to the alerting pipeline and annotates the span with 'retention_over_limit=true'.
Router handles malformed hints gracefully (logs a warning, defaults to 'hot').
End-to-end integration test demonstrating retention_hint routing for at least three tenants and verifying Tempo storage tier assignment in a synthetic Tempo test harness.
No tail-latency regression > 1ms p99 on the OTLP ingestion path after adding the router under representative load (benchmark target: 50k spans/s).
implementation_notes: Component sits as a lightweight, stateless sidecar or gateway in the OTLP ingestion path; runtime choice toggled by feature flag 'retention_router.enabled'.
Retention hint parsing: accept values as 'hot', '30d', '90d', 'archive', or ISO8601 duration (e.g., 'P90D') - normalize to canonical buckets.
Tenant quotas consulted via fast in-memory cache (LRU) of tenant retention_limits retrieved from Console API; cache TTL 30s with jittered refresh.
If tenant quota unknown, make an async call to quota service and fall back to default retention; do not block ingestion on quota lookup.
Emit a control span/envelope to a dedicated topic 'trace-control-events' when retention > quota for on-call workflows; include tenant, requested, allowed values and originating request id.
Ensure header parsing supports gRPC metadata -> map 'x-redwood-retention' to attribute when using OTLP/gRPC; support both HTTP/JSON and gRPC OTLP transports.
Auth and tenancy: enforce tenant extracted from existing authentication token; router must not accept an explicit tenant override via header unless header signature validated (future work).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated internal rollout: enable for 5 internal tenants in canary region for 48 hours; monitor latency and control-events topic.
2) Expand to subset of external beta tenants (opt-in) and run A/B validation vs baseline retention behavior for 7 days.
3) Full rollout with guardrails: default-to-normal retention for tenants without quota entries and a kill-switch in Console for immediate disable.
4) Post-rollout: schedule migration job to annotate historical spans where possible (separate ticket).
test_plan: Unit tests: parsing and normalization of retention hints, header precedence, malformed input behavior.
Integration tests: end-to-end OTLP ingest -> router -> Tempo test harness verifying tier annotation.
Load test: synthetic driver at representative span size/rate to confirm <=1ms p99 added latency.
Chaos test: simulate quota service timeouts and ensure router falls back gracefully without dropping spans.
Security review checklist: verify no privilege escalation via headers and token binding to tenant identity.
metrics: New metrics: retention_router.hits_total, retention_router.over_limit_events_total, retention_router.parse_errors_total, retention_router.latency_seconds (p50/p95/p99)
Dashboard update: Observability -> Tracing -> Retention Router (per-tenant retention distribution, over-limit alerting drilldowns)
SLOs: p99 added latency < 1ms; over-limit alert rate correlated with quota changes.
